test: Per-channel report arrival cadence, stationary mower, RTK Fix
purpose: Close the limitation recorded on 2026-08-06: the original probe counted every inbound LubaMsg and so measured total traffic, not the position-report cadence that governs overshoot.

conditions.mower: stationary at (5.0026, -3.4058), MODE_READY, blades 0, no session

method.sampling: channel payloads fingerprinted every 20 ms; an arrival is counted when a channel's fingerprint changes

finding: Messages arrived steadily at ~1.9 Hz for 40 seconds and NOT ONE carried a changed position, RTK or VIO payload. The instrumentation is not at fault: the position path is populated and a unit test drives position forward while holding RTK latched and sees exactly that split.

interpretation.leading: The device appears not to push position/RTK/VIO updates for a stationary mower -- either it suppresses unchanged values, or the ~1.9 Hz traffic is other message types entirely (keepalives, status).
interpretation.consequence: The position-report cadence CANNOT be measured from a stationary mower. The measurement the 2026-08-06 direction review needs -- how often position updates DURING motion, which bounds how precisely a stop can be timed -- requires a moving mower, daylight, and fresh operator authorization.
interpretation.not_established: Whether the device is suppressing unchanged values or simply not sending these channels. Distinguishing them needs either a moving-mower run or per-RptInfoType decoding below the pymammotion data model.

secondary_value: This probe would have caught the 2026-08-07 RTK latch in 40 seconds rather than three hours: it reports a silent channel as a finding while total traffic looks healthy, which is precisely the shape that hid the latch.
caveats: One 40-second window, one mower, stationary only.
Fingerprints are taken at the pymammotion data-model level, so a report that arrives carrying identical values is indistinguishable from a report that never arrived.
No gate is claimed and no motion ran.
